- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecasted values by 5–10% to account for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast to allow for a 1–2 day lag in price reversal.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates upside; add 3–5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price surges; increase final 5–7 days of forecast by 2–4% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model delays reaction; shift forecast upward by 1–3 days to align with sentiment shift.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, don’t assume continuation — add a 1–2 day mean-reversion buffer.
